title: MistralHealth POC: telemetry, redaction & sizing kickoff
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for MistralHealth patient triage assistant. Primary focus: PII handling and redaction approach, prompt/response logging policy, retention windows, and benchmarking for 95th percentile latency and throughput sizing. Decided next step: Redwood to share benchmark plan, security checklist, and initial config for a private VPC pilot. Customer to provide sample workload distribution and a redaction policy doc by next Tue.
action_items: Alicia Romano: Share anonymized workload profile and sample prompts (due 2026-12-01)
Jordan Hayes: Send POC benchmark plan and config template (due 2026-11-30)
Priya Desai: Prepare redaction pseudocode + sample eval harness (due 2026-12-02)
Samir Patel: Provide security questionnaire answers (due 2026-12-03)
next_steps: Redwood to run initial microbenchmarks in Redwood Dedicated with synthetic load and share results
Schedule security deep dive (30-45m) next week focused on KMS, audit logs, and SSO
Customer to confirm POC success criteria and retention window (default suggested: 7 days for prompts, 90 days for aggregated telemetry)
Plan a runbook for prompt redaction: redaction-at-ingest vs post-process approaches to be compared in POC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-28 15:00 UTC
Recorded duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Alicia Romano (MistralHealth Head of Data), Diego Marquez (CTO), Samir Patel (SecOps), Nina Ko (ML Engineer), Tom Baird (DevOps)

Auto Summary: Short scoping call to align on POC goals: privacy constraints, retention policy, benchmark metrics (95th perc latency, p99 tail), workload sizing and timeline. Agreement to share documents and run a two-step benchmark: microbench (latency, tail) then end-to-end with sample prompts.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's just do quick intros and then jump into the POC goals
[00:09] Alicia: hey this is Alicia, head of data platforms at MistralHealth, we own the triage assistant project, trying to replace a ruleset with an LLM layer, like secure and auditable
[00:18] Diego: Diego here, CTO, interested on performance and cost—want to see a path to <200ms median but realistically we care about p95 and p99 tails
[00:27] Samir: Samir (secops) - my thing is: where does PHI live, how do we stop it being logged, and how do we prove deletion for audits
[00:36] Jordan: great, and i'm Jordan from Redwood AE, with Priya and Evan from our SE team. we'll run through success criteria then telemetry/redaction options, sizing, and bench plan
[00:47] Priya: just to flag early—Redwood supports several options: hosted with strict retention, dedicated reserved capacity, or our private VPC control-plane. For POC we recommend dedicated or private to avoid noisy neighbors when measuring tail latency
[01:05] Nina: quick question - if we do private VPC, do you still store prompts in Redwood or it's customer-owned storage?
[01:12] Evan: good question. with private deployments prompts can be kept inside your VPC; with hosted we have retention controls and can opt-out of storing full prompts—often teams store hashes and minimal metadata
[01:23] Alicia: so our compliance team prefers no raw prompts kept beyond 7 days. we can accept short retention for prompts but logs with PHI must be redacted at ingestion
[01:32] Priya: we typically offer two redaction models for POC: 1) ingest-time redaction where we run a regex/NER filter before persisting, 2) post-process redaction where a copy is written to a secure bucket and redaction is applied asynchronously for auditability. both have tradeoffs for observability and debugging
[01:50] Tom: for debugging we want to keep at least some pseudonymized versions for 30 days, but samir's team wants stricter controls
[01:57] Samir: yes, auditability for our regulators but minimal exposure. can we do encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS and fine-grained access?
[02:05] Jordan: absolutely - customer-managed KMS is supported, and for private we can integrate with HSM in your cloud. access controls via RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC) are available. your audit logs can be exported to your SIEM
[02:20] Diego: how do you handle KV cache or persistent session data? That cache could leak PHI if stored wrong
[02:27] Priya: our runtime manages KV cache in-memory by default for low-latency. for longer sessions you can configure encrypted ephemeral cache or persist to customer-owned storage encrypted with KMS. when persisted we have a redaction hook to trim PHI from cached tokens
[02:44] Alicia: ok great. now on workload sizing: our current triage sees about 40 qps peak, 12 qps sustained, and average tokens per req ~950 (because of patient history snippets). can you speak to batching effects?
[02:59] Evan: so with that distribution and token lengths, batching will help throughput but can add latency. Redwood Optimize will suggest batch windows, and for POC we should test both aggressive batching (higher throughput, slightly higher median) and strict low-latency config (smaller batches). We should pick two operating points to compare.
[03:20] Nina: what's realistic p95/p99 targets given long prompts?
[03:24] Priya: with dedicated GPUs and model quantization we target p95 under 350ms for trimmed prompts and p99 under 800ms; with full 950-token context expect higher — that's why we'll run E2E benchmark with real token distribution.
[03:38] Diego: those numbers are fine as long as cost outlook is clear. show us cost per 1k tokens across configs in the benchmark results
[03:46] Jordan: noted, we'll include cost modeling. for success criteria — propose: functional parity for intent classification >95%, p95 latency <400ms for production config, redaction audit passing internal tests, and no raw PHI stored beyond agreed windows
[03:59] Alicia: yes that aligns, also want a rollback plan if we detect PHI leakage during tests
[04:05] Priya: rollback is supported — we can revert to canary model or disable logging immediately; we will propose a monitoring alert workflow in the runbook
[04:13] Samir: can you describe the benchmark plan again? especially stress profile and ingress simulation
[04:18] Evan: two stage plan: microbench - synthetic payloads with varied lengths to measure per-token latency and tail; E2E - replay of sampled anonymized prompts at scaled qps with real session patterns, including spike tests. We'll run 3 iterations and provide CSV/trace logs and per-token latency histograms
[04:36] Nina: can you capture prompt-level hashes so we can correlate failures without storing text?
[04:40] Priya: yes we can store SHA256 hashes and a minimal metadata set (len, template id, outcome) which should be sufficient for debugging and no raw content
[04:49] Diego: what about redaction accuracy? regex isn't enough, some PHI is nested in notes
[04:54] Priya: agreed - we'll include an NER-based redaction model and a manual review step for the POC. we can surface false negatives in the eval harness and tune rules. expected recall ~92% initially but we will measure on your sample set
[05:08] Alicia: what's the timeline? we want this POC done within 6 weeks if possible
[05:12] Jordan: typical 6-week plan: week 0 (this alignment), week 1-2 microbench and deploy POC infra, week 3 run E2E and redaction tuning, week 4 iteration and compliance review, week 5 final benchmark and handover. can compress but risks quality
[05:28] Tom: do you need our infra access? we prefer to keep control; can you run tests from Redwood Dedicated into our VPC with peering?
[05:36] Evan: yes we support VPC peering and a private link; or you can deploy our Private package in your subnet. Both options allow tests that meet your network policies
[05:46] Samir: on logging: we need immutable audit log exports, and ability to delete records on request within retention windows with proof of deletion
[05:55] Priya: we will provide export hooks to your SIEM and a deletion audit log. for deletion proof we'll produce event traces showing KMS key rotation and object deletion timestamps; we'll work with your legal team on the exact form required
[06:07] Diego: competitors — who else did you see doing similar for regulated healthcare?
[06:11] Jordan: many infra plays; Anthropic and OpenAI offer models but you still need infra. Vertex AI has native VPC options but less opinionated inference runtime. Redwood's differentiator is the production runtime and the integrated redaction/benchmarking toolset
[06:27] (brief crosstalk)
[06:30] Alicia: ok recap?
[06:32] Jordan: recap: deliverables from Redwood: benchmark plan (microbench + E2E), runbook for redaction and rollback, security checklist and SIEM integration steps, cost model. From MistralHealth: workload profile, redaction policy doc, sample anonymized prompts, and security questionnaire answers. Dates and owners in action items.
[06:52] Samir: one more thing - for the POC we want a legal-safe stub: redact PHI before any third-party models are hit. is that feasible?
[06:58] Priya: yes, you can run a local pre-processor or we can plug in a customer-run redaction lambda in the ingress path to ensure nothing leaves your VPC unredacted. We'll include that as an option in the runbook
[07:12] Diego: thanks, let's get the docs and schedule the security deep dive next Wed
[07:16] Jordan: perfect — we'll send invites and the benchmark plan by EOD Monday
[07:20] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms: "kayvee cache" for KV cache, "samel" for SAML, numbers sometimes merged. We left those as-is to reflect real call artifacts.

Attachments referenced: redwood-poc-benchmark-plan-v1 (link to be sent), security-checklist.pdf (to be sent), sample-runbook.md (to be shared)
